messages:

Subject: Multi-year advance commit approach / reconciliation question

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and the cost controls you showed. Before we move deeper on legal, procurement asked me to get clarity on two items for a potential 3-year advance commitment:

1) How do you handle end-of-term reconciliation? Do you do a final "reconciliation" for actual usage vs committed units, and if so how granular is it (monthly/annual/end-of-term)?

2) We often ask for a buffer band so we aren't charged for normal variability — do you offer a tolerance (e.g., +/- X%) before overage kicks in? If so, how does that interact with discounts?

We need something clear for our procurement team to sign off. Also, are you able to provide a sample term-sheet showing the discount ladder for a 3-year, declining ramp (30% year 1, 60% year 2, 100% year 3)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement would like this summarized in writing.

Best,
Hannah

Head of Platform
Acme AI

Folks — forwarding Acme's procurement questions. Quick thoughts below; want to align before I send back a formal term-sheet.

Summary of asks: end-of-term reconciliation cadence, buffer band tolerance, discount ladder for 3-year ramp.

My recommended stance:
- Reconciliation: annual true reconciliation with an end-of-term settlement (final true-up after year 3) — this keeps billing predictable but gives us a final adjustment window.
- Buffer band: propose a 10% tolerance band applied annually; usage inside band is covered by committed units. Anything above the band is billed at overage rate = list rate (no discount).
- Ramp discounts: keep discount schedule tied to committed units per year; do not retroactively apply higher-year discounts to earlier consumption.

Concessions we can be flexible on for ACME: a one-time carryforward credit if year 1 usage < 70% of committed units (up to 20% of unused units) to help them ramp. But need approval for a deeper year-1 discount.

Can you confirm margin impact (Marcus) and whether we can add the carryforward language into a term-sheet PDF (Marissa) so I can send it to Hannah?

Thanks — Nikhil

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear questions. Below is our standard approach and a proposed term sheet attached for your review. Short answers first, then details.

Short answers:
- Reconciliation cadence: annual reconciliations with a final end-of-term settlement after year 3. We invoice annually against committed units and do a final adjustment within 30 days of term-end.
- Buffer band: 10% tolerance band per-year (committed units * 0.10). Usage within the band is absorbed by the committed pool; usage above the band is billed at published overage rates.
- Discount ladder: attached (3-year example). Discounts apply to the committed units for that year. Overage is invoiced at list (no discount).

Details / optional concessions we can offer for large strategic deals:
- Carryforward credit: if year 1 actual usage is < 70% of year 1 committed units, we will allow up to 20% of the unused year-1 committed units to carry forward into year 2 as a one-time credit. This is non-transferable and expires at the end of year 2.
- Early termination: standard pro-rata refund on unused prepaid units less an administrative fee; we generally avoid guaranteed refunds on multi-year prepays.
- Audit & reporting: we provide token-level usage reports and a reconciliation workbook with the annual settlement.

I've attached a short term-sheet that captures the above and includes a sample pricing table for the ramp you mentioned. If that model looks OK, we can hand to legal and get a contract draft out.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma

Subject: Re: Multi-year advance commit approach / reconciliation question

Nikhil — thanks for the quick turnaround and the term-sheet. Procurement had two follow-ups after reviewing with finance:

1) The 10% tolerance band is acceptable, but they want to know if the overage rate could be capped at a blended rate (e.g., list * 0.9) for the first 90 days after the band is exceeded to avoid sudden bill shock during growth spurts.
2) The carryforward credit is useful — can you confirm whether the carryforward reduces the year-2 committed billing (i.e., does it reduce the invoiced committed units) or is it issued as a credit note after year-2 billing? They prefer a reduction to invoiced committed units where possible.

Also — pricing ask: Acme is pushing for a slightly higher year-1 discount (additional 3 percentage points) in exchange for signing a 36-month term now and committing to the ramp schedule you outlined. That incremental discount would be applied only to year-1 committed units.

Would Redwood be open to the 3% one-time year-1 concession plus a 90-day blended overage cap as a commercial concession for strategic cases? Procurement says that gets this over the finish line quickly.

Best,
Hannah

Subject: Request approval: Acme concession asks (3% yr1 / 90-day blended overage cap / carryforward treatment)

Team — quick summary and ask: Acme (RDW-ACME-2026-Q2) is ready to sign if we agree to three commercial concessions:
1) Increase year-1 committed discount by +3 percentage points (applies only to year-1 committed units).
2) Implement a 90-day blended overage cap at list * 0.9 that applies only to overages in the first 90 days after they exceed the 10% tolerance band (helps with growth spurts).
3) Carryforward credit: allow up to 20% of unused year-1 committed units to carry into year 2 as an invoice reduction (preferred by the customer).

Impact & recommendation (Marcus has reviewed margin):
- Margin impact is acceptable on year-1 if we limit the carryforward to invoice reduction (it avoids future credit liabilities).
- The 90-day blended cap is a short-term commercial risk but helps avoid escalation and closes the deal; recommend approving for strategic customers with a signed 3-year term.

Ask: Marissa / Lauren — can we approve the one-time 3% yr1 uplift and the 90-day blended overage cap for a signed 36-month commitment? If yes, I will send the redlined term-sheet back to Acme and ask legal to prepare the contract with the invoice-reduction language for carryforward.

Thanks — Nikhil
